scenes.title: Key ideas
items: A perpetual future (perp) tracks an asset's price with no expiry
Mark price (used for liquidation) vs index price (spot reference)
Liquidation happens when your margin falls to the maintenance margin
scenes.vo: First, A perpetual future (perp) tracks an asset's price with no expiry. You post margin and choose leverage. Next, Isolated margin: only the margin in that position is at risk. Cross margin: your whole account backs every position (one bad trade can drain the rest). Then, Mark price (used for liquidation) versus index price (spot reference). Funding is paid between longs and shorts, usually every hour or 8 hours. And finally, Liquidation happens when your margin falls to the maintenance margin. Roughly, a long is liquidated after a fall of 1 divided by leverage minus maintenance margin.

scenes.title: Worked example
steps: Long ETH from $3,000 at 5×, 0.5% maintenance margin
The same short at 20× is liquidated at ≈ $3,135 (+4.5%), a move ETH can make…
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. Long ETH from $3,000 at 5 times , 0.5% maintenance margin: the calculator gives liquidation about $2,415 (minus 19.5%). The same short at 20 times is liquidated at about $3,135 (+4.5%), a move ETH can make in an hour. Leverage doesn't just magnify gains: it shrinks how wrong you're allowed to be.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: Leverage ≤ 2–3× for anything but a hedge I fully understand
Funding cost checked for how long I'll hold
